title: Pressure induced magnetic-field-free superconducting diode effect in NbSe2 flake
authors: Shihao Zhu, Tian Le, Cuiying Pei, Changhua Li, Yi Liao, Yi Zhao, Lingxiao Zhao, Qi Wang, Juefei Wu, Qilian Zhang, Yueshen Wu, Tonghuan Fu, Xujie Lü, Wenge Yang, Jie Shen, Jun Li, Yulin Chen, Xiao Lin, Wen-Yu He, Yanpeng Qi
abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is a fascinating nonreciprocal phenomenon where the critical current is different for opposite current directions. It is widely believed that realizing SDE requires breaking both inversion symmetry (IS) and time-reversal symmetry (TRS), which are usually achieved via heterostructure engineering and applying external magnetic fields. Here, we report a pressure-induced magnetic-field-free SDE in NbSe2 flakes without any heterostructures. We show that pressure alone breaks the IS, as confirmed by the second harmonic generation. Crucially, upon applying an out-of-plane magnetic field (B), the SDE exhibits even-in-B behavior, implying the absence of explicit TRS breaking. This finding challenges the prevailing theoretical paradigm and demonstrates that a magnetic-field-free SDE can emerge without explicitly breaking TRS. Thereby, our work establishes pressure engineering as a powerful tool for inducing nonreciprocal superconductivity and designing versatile, magnetic-field-free superconducting devices.
summary: This work reports the discovery of a superconducting diode effect in $	ext{NbSe}_2$ flakes induced purely by high pressure, eliminating the need for external magnetic fields. By correlating this nonreciprocal transport with pressure-induced breaking of inversion symmetry (confirmed via SHG), the authors propose a theoretical model showing that such effects can emerge without explicitly violating time-reversal symmetry. This establishes pressure engineering as a powerful tool for realizing versatile superconducting devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the superconducting diode effect (SDE), a nonreciprocal phenomenon, aiming to challenge the conventional belief that SDE requires breaking both inversion symmetry (IS) and time-reversal symmetry (TRS).
main_result: They report observing a magnetic-field-free SDE in $	ext{NbSe}_2$ flakes using only pressure to break IS, while the effect exhibits even-in-$B$ behavior suggesting TRS preservation.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (V-I curves, SHG) under high pressure with theoretical modeling using a Landau-Ginzburg free energy functional.
model_or_system: The physical system is single-phase $	ext{NbSe}_2$ flakes studied in a Diamond Anvil Cell. The theory models the SDE origin from a cubic term ($	ext{q}^3$) coupling to the induced in-plane electric polarization after IS breaking.
key_observables:
Superconducting diode efficiency ($\eta$), nonreciprocal critical currents ($|I_{c+}| 
eq |I_{c-}|$), Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) signals, and $	ext{V-I}$ characteristics under varying pressure/field.
important_parameters: High pressures (e.g., 6.7 GPa to 15.9 GPa), low temperatures ($\sim 1.8 	ext{ K}$), and the magnetic field dependence ($B$).
main_assumptions: The primary theoretical assumption is that the SDE can arise from IS breaking via a $	ext{q}^3$ term in the free energy functional, even if TRS remains intact.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate V-I curves showing nonreciprocity under pressure (Fig. 1D), SHG patterns confirming symmetry changes ($	ext{C}_{3v} 	o 	ext{C}_{1v}$) correlating with SDE onset (Fig. 4), and the dependence of SDE on temperature and magnetic field (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first demonstrating the existence of a pressure-induced, field-free SDE in $	ext{NbSe}_2$ flakes using transport measurements; it then uses SHG to confirm the underlying symmetry breaking mechanism (IS); finally, it proposes and validates a theoretical model based on Landau-Ginzburg theory that explains the nonreciprocity without explicit TRS breaking.
why_interesting: The finding challenges established paradigms regarding superconducting diode effects by proposing a mechanism for nonreciprocity driven solely by structural symmetry breaking (pressure) rather than requiring external magnetic fields or complex heterostructures, which has implications for designing novel quantum devices.
